cim: In a first, Google detects AI-automated cyberattack
cim_eredeti: In a first, Google detects AI-automated cyberattack
szoveg_eredeti:
Nov. 17 (UPI) -- Google threat analysts said they have detected, for the first time, an artificial intelligence framework that autonomously identifies and exploits software vulnerabilities without human intervention.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group said in its quarterly report on Monday that it identified a server hosting an AI agent that autonomously searches popular web application software code for potential vulnerabilities, then drafts exploits that it executes without the involvement of a human.

Google does not explicitly attribute the framework, named exploit_agent, to any particular hackers but said it found Russian-language comments in its configuration file.

Attacks resulted in stolen data from victims, though Google did not disclose the number of organizations compromised, the nature of the information stolen or the extent of the damage.

It did say that there appeared to be a specific interest in targeting French websites associated with media and entertainment industries as well as the education sector.

The announcement comes after TIG said in its September report that it had seen "nascent efforts" by threat actors involving large language model-augmented vulnerability research.

"Threat actor adoption of these frameworks represents a paradigm shift towards intrusions occurring at machine speed," it said.

"While the mechanics of the intrusions remain the same, such as using compromised credentials and targeting unpatched systems, the speed and scale at which frameworks can exploit these known weaknesses introduces a new defensive challenge."
